issues.failure_explanation: Expanding the claimed decomposition β⊗T^(α) + β⁻¹⊗T^(1/α) with the stated three-point difference-quotient definitions of T^(α) and T^(1/α) produces a coefficient (β_p α_{q+1/2} + β_p⁻¹ α_{q+1/2}⁻¹)/Δv² on f_{p,q+1}, which does not equal the actual stencil coefficient α_{q+1/2}β_p/Δv² from eq:fp_discrete_separable. The actual decomposition requires two-point forward/backward operators T₁(w)_q = (α_{q+1/2}w_{q+1} − α_{q−1/2}w_q)/Δv² and T₂(w)_q = (w_{q−1}/α_{q−1/2} − w_q/α_{q+1/2})/Δv². Additionally, the claimed operator-norm bounds 2α_max/Δv² and 2/(α_min Δv²) are row-sum bounds correct only for these two-point operators; for the stated symmetric three-point stencils the row sums give 4α_max/Δv² and 4/(α_min Δv²). Thus the decomposition identity and the norm estimates in the proof are both inconsistent with the defined operators.

failure_location.quote:
We observe that this operator acts as a sum of tensor products involving multiplication by spatial weights $\beta$ and $\beta^{-1}$:
\[
  \mathcal{L}_{h} \;=\; \beta \otimes \mathcal{T}^{(\alpha)} \;+\; \beta^{-1} \otimes \mathcal{T}^{(1/\alpha)}.
\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace T^(α) and T^(1/α) by the two-point forward and backward difference operators that actually appear in the decomposition of the stencil (eq:fp_discrete_separable), and adjust the norm estimates accordingly (the same numerical bounds 2α_max/Δv² and 2/(α_min Δv²) then hold for the corrected operators). The rest of the proof strategy and the conclusion κ_h remain unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Proposition 2 as written does not establish the projection bound ‖(I−P_X)ℒ_h(f)‖ ≤ κ_h‖f‖ because the central algebraic identity (the operator decomposition) is false and the accompanying norm estimates do not match the operators defined. The stated constant κ_h and the proposition's conclusion remain correct when the proof is redone with the correct two-point decomposition, but the proof as written is invalid.
issues.title: Incorrect tensor-product decomposition of the discrete Fokker–Planck operator in Proposition 2 proof
issues.why_classification: The repair requires replacing the operator decomposition with a different (non-equivalent) set of velocity difference operators and re-deriving the norm bounds for them, which is more than a single local correction but remains a contained revision within the existing proof architecture. The proposition's statement and constant κ_h survive unchanged, so no result is lost.
